content.intro: {state} charges {stateRate} state sales tax on a vehicle, and cities or counties may add their own tax. Registration fees are small, but a yearly motor vehicle tax based on the original price is billed at registration.

howItWorks.text: The state rate is {stateRate}. The tax is figured on the price minus any trade-in allowance and any rebates that lower the selling price.
Local sales tax can be added on top. Your county treasurer can tell you the rate for your location.
If you paid a lower sales tax in the state where you bought, Nebraska collects the difference when you register.
The state also bills a motor vehicle tax each year. It is based on the vehicle's original price and drops as the vehicle ages, so it is not part of this total.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the sales tax in Nebraska?
faq.text: Yes. The state's rule says the tax is figured on the sales price minus the trade-in allowance and any rebates used to reduce the selling price.

faq.q: Is the yearly motor vehicle tax included?
faq.text: No. It depends on the vehicle's original price and age, and it is billed at the first registration and every year after.

faq.q: Do electric vehicles pay an extra fee?
faq.text: Yes. Electric and hydrogen fuel cell passenger vehicles pay an alternative fuel fee on top of registration.
